title: The HTTP request target does not contain a fragment of the URL
summary: After the browser parses the URL, the fragment starting with # is processed by the client and is not sent to the server along with the request target.
applies: Browser interpretation of URLs, cookies, and origins
detail: When two history URLs differ only in fragments, it is possible to see the exact same path and query in the server access log.
boundary: The percent-encoded %23 is data within the corresponding URL component; it should be determined during the correct parsing phase.
relevance: Compare the address bar, HAR, and access logs to determine which piece of information is only visible on the client.
